quote: As a traditional Japanese restaurant relying on dashi, soy sauce and seasoned broths, dishes here almost certainly use wheat-containing soy sauce; no allergy or gluten information is published.
found: Own お品書き/ランチ menu, verbatim: 「ごきげん巻とうどん 1,500円」「ちらし寿しとうどん 2,200円」「にぎりと紙鍋うどん 2,800円」「海鮮カレーうどん 1,650円」「上天丼 2,800円」「まめ福コロッケ定食 1,700円」「古処鶏からあげ定食 1,700円」「車海老食パンチーズ巻揚 2,640円」「穴子の焼霜造り又白焼又かば焼き」「めばるの煮付」「わけぎのぬた和え」「海鮮カレーライス」. No allergen or gluten text appears anywhere on the site.
note: The claim is true but far weaker than the evidence. The record hedges on 'almost certainly ... soy sauce' while this venue's own menu prints outright wheat in four udon dishes, tempura/上天丼, korokke, karaage, Japanese curry roux and 車海老食パンチーズ巻揚 — a prawn wrapped in 食パン (white bread). Rewrite the claim around the named udon/tempura/bread items; a celiac needs the hard facts, not an inference about tare. gf 'no' is correct.

quote: The menu is fish- and seafood-centered with dashi-based seasoning throughout, so vegan diners would face fish stock and animal ingredients in most dishes.
